title: Batch scheduler mutex deadlock: field notes and triage
content:
Summary:

Observed inter-host stalls and full request hang across a subset of hosts in the serving fleet over the 2025-02-14 02:00–04:30 UTC window. Symptoms: very high p95/p99 generation latency, long living inflight requests > 60s, and hosts reported CPU stuck in user-space threads tied to scheduler code. No OOMs or host-level memory pressure during the incident. Multiple tenants affected but high correlation with workloads using continuous batching and long prompt prefixes.

Why this doc exists (notes to self):
- Capture a timeline with logs and quick repro steps.
- Draft temporary mitigation steps that can be applied without full deploy.
- Propose a runbook entry and follow-ups for the batching scheduler and mutex design.
- Keep short, actionable steps for on-call.

High-level hypothesis (working):
- A recent scheduler change (PR#512) introduced a backoff and 'hold for network I/O' optimization which accidentally allows the per-batch mutex (batch_coordinator::batch_lock) to be held across a remote KV prefetch path.
- When host swap or remote KV rebuild occurs, that prefetch path can block on cross-host RPCs while still holding batch_lock. Another thread on a different host attempts to acquire the same logical lock via the distributed coordinator (via lease semantics) causing a circular dependency: local thread A holds lock and waits on remote RPC to host B; thread B holds a different resource and is waiting on an event from A -> deadlock across hosts.
- Evidence: stack traces show batch_lock held, top frames reference scheduler::submit_batch -> prefetch_client::await_response. Metrics show spike in prefetch RPC latency to ~500–1200ms prior to stall.

Timeline (concise):
- 2025-02-14 01:58 UTC: Canary deploy of PR#512 to region-us-east-1 (automated rollout, 10% hosts).
- 2025-02-14 02:10 UTC: Alert: batch-queue-depth spikes on group A; p95 latency climbs.
- 02:17 UTC: Several hosts go into 'hang' state; on-call triggered.
- 02:30 UTC: Manual rollback of PR#512 started; observed partial recovery over next 30–60 minutes as canary hosts drained.
- 03:20 UTC: Full rollback complete; service metrics returned to baseline by 03:40 UTC.

Quick evidence snapshot (logs/snippets):
- /var/log/runtime/serving.log snippet: 
  [2025-02-14T02:12:03Z] ERROR scheduler.cpp:237 hold_batch_lock pid=7523 tid=140 prefetch_client.cc:412 waiting for remote-kv host=kv-12.us-east-1: rpc_send timeout
- gdb stack on hung thread: 
  scheduler::submit_batch()
  -> batch_coordinator::hold_lock()
  -> prefetch_client::await_response()
  -> rpc::network::poll()
- Prometheus: prefetch_rpc_duration_seconds_bucket{le="1.0"} spiked from 0.02 to 0.35 for top hosts.

Short-term mitigation (on-call playbook):
1) Identify affected hosts: query graphite/prometheus for hosts with active_inflight_requests > 20 and batch_lock_hold_ms > 2000.
   - Command: curl -s 'http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=active_inflight_requests%7Bjob%3D%22serving%22%7D%20%3E%2020' | jq .
2) If PR#512 is in rollout, stop the rollout and pin the previous version (rollback).
   - GitHub action: revert the canary deploy or set dynconfig rollout.enabled=false for the batch scheduler.
3) For hosts in hung state, prefer a graceful drain: set /_admin/drain?t=30s on the node and monitor in-flight decrease. If drain stalls, escalate to immediate restart of the runtime process.
   - Command: curl -XPOST http://<host>:9090/_admin/drain?timeout=30s
4) If multiple hosts are hung and cross-host deadlock suspected, avoid restarting all at once. Restart in subsets and verify the distributed lease releases before continuing.

Runbook draft entry (to add to canonical runbook):
- Incident name: Inter-host batch mutex deadlock (scheduler hold across KV RPC)
- Trigger conditions: sustained batch_lock_hold_ms > 1000ms and concurrent increase in prefetch_rpc_duration_seconds and inflight_request_count
- Immediate actions: follow short-term mitigation above.
- Persistent mitigation: back out PR changes that hold scheduler mutex across I/O; instrument stronger assertions that batch_lock is not held while performing network syscalls.
- Long-term: redesign batch_lock to use an acquisition token that can be released before network I/O or split responsibilities so local scheduling doesn't call blocking prefetch paths while holding global coordination locks.

Reproduction steps (dev/local lab):
- Environment: spin up 3-node mini-cluster with full KV simulation that can inject artificial RPC latency and host-swap events.
- Patch: enable PR#512 behavior (scheduler backoff) and insert latency injector to kv-*-sim of 600–1200ms for a subset of keys.
- Load: run continuous-batching workload with long prefix lengths (>= 1024 tokens) and high concurrency (~200 qps across cluster).
- Expected: within minutes, some worker threads will show batch_lock held while prefetch RPC is inflight, leading to circular waits across nodes.

Instrumenting for future detection (metrics & alerts):
- New metric: batch_lock_hold_ms per host histogram (already partially present; ensure sum and count exported). Alert when p99 > 2000ms for 5m.
- Correlate with prefetch_rpc_duration_seconds per host. Create a composite alert: batch_lock_p99>2000ms AND prefetch_rpc_p95>500ms.
- Tracing: add a trace span for "batch_lock.acquire" and ensure network RPC spans are sibling/child spans so we can see hold durations where the lock is held across network calls.

Suggested immediate code checks (for eng):
- Grep for 'hold_lock' or 'batch_lock' usages and mark any callsites that potentially perform network I/O. Add DEBUG-ASSERT to fail fast in staging if batch_lock is held across an RPC.
- Add deterministic unit tests in scheduler that simulate slow prefetch client to ensure lock isn't held.

Follow-ups and ownership:
- Owner for fix: Marcus Nguyen (sre + serving-runtime pairing) -> coordinate with infra/serving-runtime team.
- Fix needs: roll back PR#512, land a patch to ensure batch_lock is not held across prefetch or use non-blocking prefetch attachment.
- Postmortem owner: Aisha Patel (compile timeline, include logs and metric graphs).
- Test owner: Lena Müller (integration test harness & latency injectors).

Action items (short checklist):
- [x] Rollback PR#512 rollout (02:30 UTC)
- [ ] Add assertion to scheduler code to detect lock-across-io in staging
- [ ] Create composite alert for batch_lock + prefetch latency
- [ ] Add runbook section and playbook commands (this doc -> canonical runbook)
- [ ] Integration test with artificial slow-kv and long-prefix workload

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did only some hosts become deadlocked during canary (difference in network topology or KV partitioning?)
- Is there any interaction with host-level TCP queue saturation or kernel-level socket buffers that amplifies the prefetch latency?
- Could tenant request patterns (very long prefix + low variability) systematically trigger scheduler paths that expose the race?

Notes for on-call (concise, copyable):
- If you see batch_lock_hold_ms p99 > 2s and prefetch_rpc_p95 > 500ms, pause canary and start draining affected hosts. Avoid mass restarts.
- Use flag: scheduler.continuous_batching.enabled=false to temporarily disable continuous batching per-dynconfig.
- Contact owners: Marcus Nguyen (pager), Lena Müller (test harness), Aisha Patel (postmortem).

Appendix (quick commands and queries):
- Prometheus: top hung hosts by lock hold time:
  curl -s 'http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=topk(5,batch_lock_hold_ms%5B5m%5D)' | jq .
- Active in-flight per host:
  curl -s 'http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=active_inflight_requests%7Bjob%3D%22serving%22%7D' | jq .
- Force drain endpoint:
  curl -XPOST http://HOST:9090/_admin/drain?timeout=30s
- Safety: to avoid split-brain, do not restart >25% of cluster hosts in the same availability zone at once.

End notes:
- This is a rough field notebook. Move accepted items into the canonical runbook and code fixes into a tracked Jira with link. Keep this doc for quick reference during follow-ups.

-- Aisha
